metric_info.time_weighted_return: Time-weighted return (TWR) shows how your investments did, as if you never added or withdrew money. Use it to compare with an index. From one year on, it is also shown as a yearly rate.
metric_info.money_weighted_return: Money-weighted return (MWR) shows what your money actually earned, counting when you added or withdrew it: the one rate of growth that turns what you put in, less what you took out, into what you have now. From one year on, it is also shown as a yearly rate.
metric_info.simple_return: Simple return compares total gain or loss with net contributions. It is cumulative and not time weighted.
metric_info.return_on_cost: Return on investment (ROI) compares your gain with the money you put in. Accounts tracked by holdings use it over their full history, and portfolios that include one use it for every period, because deposits and withdrawals are not recorded there.
metric_info.price_return: Price return measures the selected symbol's price change over the selected period.
metric_info.benchmark_money_weighted: The benchmark's money-weighted return with your own deposits and withdrawals replayed into it: what your money would have earned there, on the same dates. Prices only, without currency effects.
metric_info.volatility: Volatility measures the dispersion of returns for a given investment. Higher volatility means the investment can change dramatically over a short period. It is annualized from calendar-daily returns.
metric_info.max_drawdown: Maximum Drawdown represents the largest percentage decline from a peak to a subsequent trough in portfolio value during the specified period. It indicates downside risk.
metric_info.annualized_return: Annualized return is the average yearly compounded rate for the selected period. It is not the cumulative total gain or loss.
metric_info.holdings_volatility: Volatility of account value changes. Based on daily valuations without adjusting for deposits or withdrawals. Reflects how much the market value fluctuates.
metric_info.holdings_max_drawdown: Largest peak-to-trough decline in account value. Based on daily valuations without adjusting for deposits or withdrawals.
